1.bug_scenario: The user has a simple HTML template with a placeholder comment inside a <script> tag. They read in another JS file’s contents (which may include the sequence `$'`) and do a plain String.replace(placeholder, scriptString) to inject it. In JavaScript’s replace API, `$'` in the replacement string is interpreted as “everything after the match,” so any occurrence of `$'` in the injected script causes the remainder of the template (including the closing <\/script> tag) to be swallowed or injected incorrectly. In the browser’s devtools you see the injected code escaping the script block, the rest of the page missing, and a truncated HTML structure.
